primary.title: The Akbarnama
primary.author: Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak
primary.rationale: This is the official biography of Akbar, commissioned by Akbar himself and written by his courtier Abu'l-Fazl. It provides extensive details on his life, reign, and administration.

primary.title: Ain-i-Akbari
primary.author: Abu'l-Fazl ibn Mubarak
primary.rationale: A detailed administrative and cultural encyclopaedia of Akbar's empire, also compiled by Abu'l-Fazl under Akbar's patronage. It covers various aspects of governance, economy, and society.

secondary.title: Akbar: The Great Mughal
secondary.author: J.L. Mehta
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive and scholarly biography of Akbar, widely cited in historical research on the Mughal Empire.

secondary.title: Akbar and the Uttam
secondary.author: Iqtidar Alam Khan
secondary.rationale: This article delves into specific aspects of Akbar's reign, likely focusing on his policies or interactions with certain groups, offering scholarly analysis.

secondary.title: Mughal Administration
secondary.author: Radha Krishna Das
secondary.rationale: While the publication year is exactly 1976, this book is a foundational text for understanding Mughal administrative structures, which were heavily shaped by Akbar's reign.

suggestions.notes: Direct primary sources authored by Akbar himself are rare. His reign is primarily documented through court historians and official chronicles like the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari, which were commissioned and patronized by him. These are considered primary sources due to their direct connection to his court and era.
